- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off or market weakness.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 1–2% of spike height.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check sentiment for bearish signals — if present, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast to align with recent trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1 → 0.9), model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
